reason: The hypothesis makes specific claims about oxide formation, diffusion control, stress evolution, and spallation behaviour for Al, Si, and Mn in CrFeCoNiX alloys, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the synergistic oxide behaviour or stress/diffusion mechanisms in these specific high-entropy alloy compositions under the stated conditions.
premises: Al or Si in CrFeCoNiX forms thermodynamically stable Al2O3 or SiO2 alongside Cr2O3
Al2O3/SiO2 + Cr2O3 scale limits outward cation flux and minimizes internal stresses
Mn in CrFeCoNiX forms less protective, more volatile Mn oxides
Mn oxides lead to rapid scale growth, higher stress, cracking and spallation
The oxide scale's diffusion-barrier and stress-control properties govern protective-layer persistence above 900 °C
